questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “body” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Curd cut into small pieces gives up more whey than curd left in large ones, and the drier the curd the firmer the cheese that comes of it. A maker who wants a paste that slices without crumbling will cut fine and press hard; one aiming at something that spreads under a knife will do neither. Almost every decision at the vat is taken with the <u>body</u> of the finished cheese in view.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The main part of a written text.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A group of people organised for a purpose.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The physical consistency of a substance.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A quantity of matter of no fixed shape.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: When more than two candidates stand, a plurality count can hand the seat to someone most voters ranked last. A ballot that asks voters to rank the whole field allows the weakest candidate to be eliminated and those ballots passed to each voter's next name, and the count repeats until somebody holds a majority. The procedure treats a first preference for a losing candidate as _____ rather than as a vote thrown away.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An expedition that flies to a base at four thousand metres and starts for the top the next morning will lose most of its members to headache and vomiting inside two days. Parties that instead carry loads to a higher camp and come back down to sleep gain height far more slowly, and the body has time to settle into a faster resting breath and a thicker blood. Success on a high peak is therefore _____ rather than a matter of pace.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A building set on bearings of layered rubber and lead is not braced against an earthquake so much as separated from it. The bearings are soft enough sideways that the ground can travel a foot beneath the structure while the floors above sway slowly and stay together. The design works by making the connection between ground and building deliberately _____.

questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “stand” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A forester walking a hillside records the species, the average diameter and the range of ages on each parcel before writing a management plan. Two parcels carrying the same species may still be handled quite differently: an even-aged <u>stand</u> planted after a clearance is thinned on a schedule, while one holding trees of many ages is worked tree by tree.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A piece of furniture for holding objects.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A group of trees growing together on one site.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A halt in movement or growth.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A signal box controls both the signals that give a driver permission to proceed and the levers that move the points beneath the track. Left to itself the arrangement lets a signalman clear a route while the points at the far end still lie for a different one. Nineteenth-century engineers answered this by locking the levers to one another in a frame of bars and notches, so that a signal cannot be pulled off unless every point in its route is already set and locked.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To describe a hazard in early signalling and the mechanical answer devised for it.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To argue that mechanical frames were superior to the electrical systems that followed them.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To explain how points are moved beneath a running line.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To trace the career of a nineteenth-century signalling engineer.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A graduate student assembling a radio survey in 1967 noticed a smear of signal returning in the same patch of sky. High-speed recordings resolved it into pulses arriving one and a third seconds apart, steadier than any clock then in service. The team spent months eliminating radar, unsuppressed car ignitions and the possibility of a message from another civilisation before settling on a natural source: a collapsed star spinning on its axis and sweeping a beam past the Earth.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To recount how an unexplained signal was tracked down to a natural source.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To argue that radio surveys are more productive than optical ones.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To explain how a collapsed star comes to spin so rapidly.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To describe the instruments used in radio surveys of the 1960s.

questions.stem: According to the text, why do wheels ripened cold lack holes?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The round holes in a wheel of Alpine cheese are bubbles of gas that formed while the wheel sat in a warm room. A bacterium the makers tolerate feeds on the lactic acid left behind by the starter cultures and gives off carbon dioxide, and the paste at that stage is elastic enough to stretch around the gas rather than crack. Wheels ripened cold from the first day contain the same bacterium and stay solid.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The starter cultures leave no lactic acid behind in them.

choices.label: B
choices.content: They are made without the bacterium responsible for producing the gas.

choices.label: C
choices.content: They are never given the warmth the bacterium needs to produce gas.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Their paste is too elastic to hold a bubble open.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Fish and crayfish shut into cave streams for many generations lose their eyes and their colour, and the loss is not simply neglect: in some cave fish the tissue that would become an eye begins to form in the embryo and is then broken down again. Eyes are expensive to build and to run, and in permanent darkness they return nothing. Related populations that still meet daylight at a cave mouth keep both eyes and colour.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Cave fish and cave crayfish are more closely related to one another than to surface species.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Populations living at a cave mouth will lose their eyes in time as well.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Cave animals lose their eyes because darkness prevents their embryos from developing normally.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The loss of eyes in cave animals reflects the cost of maintaining a useless organ rather than mere disuse.

questions.stem: Which quotation from Ulf's verses most effectively illustrates the scholar's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Skaldic poetry names things by compound substitution: a ship becomes a horse of the sea, gold the fire of the river. A scholar argues that in the verses attributed to the tenth-century poet Ulf the Silent these substitutions are not decoration but a means of forcing two unlike activities to be seen as one.

choices.label: A
choices.content: “We sowed the sea-field with oars and reaped a harvest of salt; the ploughman ashore knows nothing of that tillage.”

choices.label: B
choices.content: “Ulf made this verse in the winter that the ice came early.”

choices.label: C
choices.content: “Gold is called the fire of the river by the poets of the north.”

choices.label: D
choices.content: “The wave-horse ran, and the sail was wide.”

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Bergström's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Wells drawing on one aquifer interfere with each other: pumping at one lowers the water table at the next. Economist Hana Bergström argues that the fall in the water table beneath one irrigation district was halted by the metering and transferable pumping quota introduced there, rather than by the run of wetter years that began at about the same time.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Rainfall across the region in the years after the quota was introduced was above the long-term average.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Farmers in the district traded a quarter of the quota among themselves in the first three years.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The aquifer is recharged mainly by rain falling on its outcrop at the edge of the district.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Neighbouring districts drawing on the same aquifer, which had the same wetter years but no metering, went on losing water table at the earlier rate.

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Duarte's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A midge beats its wings a thousand times a second, far faster than a nerve can deliver separate commands. Entomologist Rafael Duarte argues that the wingbeat rate is set by the mechanical resonance of the thorax rather than by the rate at which signals arrive at the muscle.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Midges beat their wings more slowly in cold air than in warm air.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A midge that loses part of one wing flies in circles.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Gluing a trace of extra mass to the wings lowers the wingbeat rate by exactly the amount a resonating system predicts, while the rate of nerve signals to the muscle is unchanged.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The thorax of a midge is a stiff box whose walls are deformed by the flight muscle.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A radio dish focuses the waves it collects only if its surface departs from a true paraboloid by much less than the wavelength being observed. Panels can be set to within a fraction of a millimetre, but a large dish also sags under its own weight as it tips, and the sag changes with the angle at which it is pointed. A dish built to work at centimetre wavelengths can therefore be enlarged much further than one intended for _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: wavelengths of a millimetre or less.

choices.label: D
choices.content: the same wavelengths at a fixed elevation.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Air moves in and out of some caves through a single small opening, at times hard enough to be heard. The direction depends on the difference between the temperature inside, which stays near the local annual mean all year, and the temperature outside. Cavers who feel cold air pouring steadily out of a crack in a limestone hillside in August can reasonably conclude that the crack opens into _____

choices.label: C
choices.content: a passage that has been surveyed before.

choices.label: D
choices.content: a space of substantial volume beyond it.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A rorqual takes in a volume of water larger than its own body in one lunge and then forces it out again through the baleen. The throat is built for exactly that _____ running from the chin to the navel and opening like a bellows under the load.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An earthquake warning system predicts nothing; it detects the fast compressional wave at stations near the source and sends word ahead of the slower shaking that does the damage. Where the distance is short — a city standing almost on the fault, for _____ arrives too late to be of any use.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A deed written by metes and bounds walks the reader around a parcel from one landmark to the next, and the landmarks were often perishable. The surveyors sent west after 1785 worked instead from a system that needed no landmarks at _____ north–south principal meridian, an east–west base line, and townships six miles square counted off from where the two cross.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Rivers carried timber out of country that had no roads, and a mill could stand a hundred miles below the felling. The river driver, a man who walked the moving logs with a pole and a pair of spiked _____ the jams apart at the head of the run and rode the loose wood down.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The mill runs two shifts and stops only to change a blade. Each of the four saws _____ its own set of guides and a jet of water to carry the sawdust away.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The church has been shut since a survey found the tower leaning, and the grant took four years to obtain. The money is to tie the walls to the floors, to grout the rubble core and _____ the roof to the masonry beneath it.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The hut warden keeps a log of every party that goes up and comes back down, and the entries are checked each evening against the boots left in the porch. Neither the guide nor the two clients _____ signed the book on the morning they set out for the col.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: An observatory can shelter from transmitters on the ground by sitting in a valley and asking its neighbours to switch things off. _____ satellite constellations broadcast from directly overhead, where no hill stands between the transmitter and the dish.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A street planted with a single species matures evenly, and every tree along it can be pruned on the same cycle. _____ a disease that finds one of those trees will find all of them, which is what happened to the elms of North American cities in the middle of the twentieth century.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Brunel laid his line to a gauge of just over seven feet, and his carriages rode more steadily than those on the narrower track used elsewhere. _____ every wagon reaching the boundary between the two systems had to be unloaded and its contents carried across to another wagon.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how the electric instruments improved on the staff-and-ticket arrangement. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A single line worked in both directions can carry a head-on collision if two trains are admitted at once.
  • Under the staff-and-ticket system only the driver holding a metal staff could enter the section.
  • A second train could follow the first if the signalman showed the staff and issued a paper ticket.
  • Electric token instruments were introduced in the 1880s and hold a set of tokens at each end of the section.
  • The instruments are wired so that only one token can be out of the machines at any moment.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Under the staff-and-ticket system only the driver holding a metal staff could enter the section.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Electric token instruments were introduced in the 1880s and hold a set of tokens at each end of the section.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Because the instruments are wired so that only one token can leave them at a time, the electric system enforced through machinery a rule that staff and ticket had left in the signalman's keeping.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A single line worked in both directions can carry a head-on collision if two trains are admitted at once.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the newer tests were developed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A legislative map can be drawn to favour one party while giving every district an equal population.
  • Courts have often asked whether a district is compact in shape.
  • One compactness score divides a district's area by the area of the smallest circle enclosing it.
  • A coastline or a winding river can give an honestly drawn district a very low score.
  • Newer tests compare a proposed map with thousands of maps generated at random under the same rules.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A legislative map can be drawn to favour one party while giving every district an equal population.

choices.label: B
choices.content: One compactness score divides a district's area by the area of the smallest circle enclosing it.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Because a shape score penalises districts that merely follow a coastline or a winding river, the newer tests judge a map against thousands of alternatives drawn under the same rules instead.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Courts have often asked whether a district is compact in shape.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the older framework had to be replaced. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Australia sits on a plate that moves about seven centimetres a year to the north-east.
  • The national coordinate framework was last fixed to the ground in 1994.
  • By 2020 positions measured by satellite differed from the 1994 framework by about 1.8 metres.
  • Machinery that steers itself by satellite works to a few centimetres.
  • A new framework was adopted that states where a point will lie in 2020 and how fast it is moving.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The national coordinate framework was last fixed to the ground in 1994.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Because the continent had drifted about 1.8 metres from its 1994 positions, a framework fixed in that year could no longer serve machinery that steers itself to a few centimetres.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A new framework was adopted that states where a point will lie in 2020 and how fast it is moving.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Australia sits on a plate that moves about seven centimetres a year to the north-east.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A levelling crew works from a mark of known height to a new one and then runs the whole line back to where it began. If the readings do not return to the height they started from, the difference is spread through the intermediate points in proportion to the distance between them. The return run is therefore a way of _____ the work rather than merely repeating it.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Han envoys sent west in the second century BCE came back with accounts of horses in the Ferghana valley taller than anything bred on the steppe and said to sweat blood. The court wanted them for its cavalry and in the end sent an army to fetch them. For the emperor the animals were less a curiosity than a _____, since mounted archers on the northern frontier could not be met on foot.

questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “solution” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Limestone is barely soluble in pure water, but rain that has taken up carbon dioxide from the air and from soil turns weakly acidic and carries the rock away in dissolved form. Caves in a limestone hill are not ground out; the passages are widened by <u>solution</u> along joints that were already there, at a rate of a few centimetres in a thousand years.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The process by which a solid is dissolved in a liquid.

choices.label: B
choices.content: A liquid mixture used for cleaning.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The breaking apart of rock by force.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: No single dish can be built wide enough to show detail on the scale radio astronomers want. The signals from many small dishes spread over miles of ground are recorded with exact timing and combined afterwards, and the array then behaves as though it were one instrument as wide as the distance between its outermost dishes. Resolution on this scale is _____ rather than built.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Air over a paved square on a July afternoon can stand several degrees warmer than the air a hundred metres away under a row of mature planes. Shade accounts for part of the gap; the rest comes from water drawn up through the trees and released from their leaves, which consumes heat as it evaporates. A large canopy therefore does not merely block the sun but _____ the air around it.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The rings of a single tree record the growing conditions of one place, and a run of narrow rings marks a run of poor years. <u>Because those poor years fall in the same order in every tree in a district, a sequence of rings taken from a beam of unknown date can be slid along a sequence from living trees until the two patterns coincide.</u> A roof timber can be dated this way to the year the tree was felled, provided its outermost ring survives.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It defines the term used for a run of narrow rings.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It explains the matching procedure that makes the dating in the final sentence possible.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It concedes a limitation that the final sentence goes on to remove.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It gives an example of a district in which the method has been used.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Calculations that treat an insect wing as a small aeroplane wing yield a lift too small to hold the animal up, and for years the discrepancy was repeated as a curiosity. <u>A wing sweeping through air at a steep angle sheds a spiral of air that clings to its upper surface instead of peeling away, and the low pressure inside that spiral pulls the wing upward.</u> Because the stroke reverses before the spiral can detach, the insect never loses the extra lift.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It restates the calculation reported in the first sentence in simpler terms.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It concedes that the discrepancy has never been explained.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It describes an experiment in which insect wings were measured.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It introduces the mechanism that accounts for the discrepancy described in the first sentence.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Every male humpback in an ocean basin sings the same song, and the song drifts through the season as small alterations spread from one singer to the next. Recordings off eastern Australia show a song replaced outright within a single season by one that had been current further west, and the replacement then travelled eastward across the Pacific over the years that followed. The new song was not a variation on the old one: the population dropped what it had been singing and took up the arriving version whole.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Each humpback develops a song of its own that changes as the animal ages.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Humpback song is learned and can be replaced wholesale by a version arriving from another population.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Humpback whales sing chiefly in order to defend a feeding territory.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Songs recorded off eastern Australia are longer than those recorded further west.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A yurt travels on two or three animals and is raised by two people in about an hour. Its wall is a lattice of pivoted laths that opens like a concertina and is drawn closed by a woven band; the roof poles spring from the top of that lattice to a wooden crown, and the felt goes on over the whole. Nothing in the frame is nailed, and it is the tension in the band that keeps the roof poles seated.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A yurt is raised more quickly in summer than in winter.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The wooden crown is the part of a yurt most often replaced.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The yurt's frame is held together by tension rather than by fixed joints, which is what makes it portable.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The felt covering is the heaviest part of a yurt to transport.

questions.stem: Which quotation from The Ash Fall most effectively illustrates the critic's claim?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: In the novel The Ash Fall, a young geologist returns to the farm she left as a child and spends her first days walking the moraine above it. A critic argues that the narrator's close attention to rock and weather is a way of putting off the conversation she has come home to have.

choices.label: A
choices.content: “The farm was smaller than I remembered, and the roof had been mended with sheeting that did not match.”

choices.label: B
choices.content: “My mother asked what I had been doing on the hill, and I told her about the meltwater until she laughed.”

choices.label: C
choices.content: “Ash from the eruption lay across the pasture in a grey band a finger deep.”

choices.label: D
choices.content: “The moraine was well sorted, the cobbles laid down by meltwater rather than dropped from the ice, and I catalogued them all afternoon while my mother waited in the kitchen.”

questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sæther's argument?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Climbers who spend a fortnight above 5,000 metres lose muscle even when they are generously fed. Physiologist Ingrid Sæther argues that the loss is caused by the shortage of oxygen itself rather than by the reduced appetite that also sets in at altitude.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Cold slows the rate at which muscle protein is rebuilt.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Volunteers held for a fortnight in a low-oxygen chamber at sea level, on a diet they finished in full each day, lost muscle at the same rate as climbers at altitude.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Climbers at altitude report eating roughly a third fewer calories than they do at home.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Muscle lost during an expedition is regained within a few weeks of the return to sea level.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the conclusion that the climbers were adjusting to the altitude over the five days?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
A physiologist measured resting arterial oxygen saturation and resting breathing rate in four climbers on each of five mornings spent at a camp at 4,900 metres, with no further gain in height during the study. Saturation at sea level is normally about 98 per cent.
Day at 4,900 mMean saturation (%)Mean breaths per minute
18220
28422
38623
48823

choices.label: A
choices.content: Mean saturation on every day of the study was below the sea-level figure of about 98 per cent.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Mean breathing rate was the same on the third, fourth and fifth days.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Mean saturation on the fifth day was 89 per cent.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Mean saturation rose from 82 per cent on the first day to 89 per cent on the fifth while the height of the camp stayed the same.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A steel rail lengthens by about a centimetre in every hundred metres for each ten degrees it warms. Jointed track left a gap at each rail end to take that movement, at the cost of a hammering that wore out rail and wheel alike. Continuous welded rail has no gaps; the rails are instead stretched to a set tension as they are fastened down, which means that track of this kind can only be laid _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: on ballast that traffic has already packed.

choices.label: B
choices.content: within a defined range of temperature.

choices.label: C
choices.content: where the line runs straight for long distances.

choices.label: D
choices.content: by machine rather than by hand.

questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Satellite positioning returns heights measured from a smooth mathematical ellipsoid fitted to the planet as a whole. Water, however, settles according to gravity, and gravity varies with the rock beneath: the surface gravity defines rises over dense mountain roots and falls over deep sedimentary basins, departing from the ellipsoid by as much as a hundred metres. An engineer laying a canal that must run downhill the whole way therefore cannot rely on _____

choices.label: A
choices.content: any height measured more than a century ago.

choices.label: B
choices.content: the precision of modern satellite positioning.

choices.label: C
choices.content: a survey carried out with satellite receivers alone.

choices.label: D
choices.content: measurements taken during the winter months.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A right to divert water in the western states is held only for as long as the water is actually put to a use the law counts as beneficial. A farmer who lines a leaking ditch and needs less water as a result may find the saved portion forfeit rather than _____ rule written to stop hoarding now discourages the very efficiency it was meant to encourage.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A rule that compares candidates in pairs can return a majority for one candidate over a second, for the second over a third, and for the third over the first. When those three results are set out in a _____ candidate can be said to have beaten every rival, and the rule produces no winner at all.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Most limestone caves are dissolved from above by rain made weakly acid in the soil. Lechuguilla was dissolved from below, and the evidence consists of three features found nowhere in an ordinary _____ blocks of gypsum left behind as a residue, sulphur crusts on the walls, and passages that climb instead of following the water table.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING

choices.label: A
choices.content: Every cheese in the store has a maturing loss of between 112 grams and 124 grams.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The mean maturing loss for all 900 cheeses in the store is certainly 118 grams.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Nothing about the store as a whole can be concluded, because only 60 cheeses were weighed.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It is plausible that the mean maturing loss for all 900 cheeses in the store is between 112 grams and 124 grams.
